newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar agrees on interim LNG price for Japan.
newsitem.headline: Qatar agrees on interim LNG price for Japan.

text.p: Qatar has agreed on an interim price of $4.10 per million British Thermal Unit for liquefied natural gas it is supplying to Japan, a newspaper said on Sunday.

"We agreed on an interim price (of $4.10) as it would provide buyers with an incentive to settle a long-term market price," the English-language daily the Peninsula quoted an official at Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas) as saying.
The CIF price offer was made by five Japanese customers led by Chubu Electric Power Company and was valid for three months to March 31.
The two sides would meet again in the last week of February to discuss a long-term price, the official said.

Qatargas has signed a sales-and-purchase agreement to supply four million tonnes a year of LNG to Chubu for 25 years from January 1997 and two million tonnes a year to seven other Japanese utilities for the same period from mid-1998 on a "take-or-pay" term.
Supplies to Chubu began on January 10 when a tanker delivered 135,000 cubic metres (63,000 tonnes) of LNG at Chubu's Nagoya gas terminal.
But under the deal, determination of the price of gas has been left to periodical reviews based on the changing prices of other competing sources of energy, like crude oil.
However, a floor price of $3.60 per million BTU is guaranteed to ensure that the grassroot project keeps running.
The official told the newspaper the interim price was approved after the two sides failed to reach an agreement on a long-term market price at their earlier meetings.
"We are relieved at having arrived at an interim delivered price and look forward to the next round of talks," said the official.
Qatargas is one of the oil and gas-rich state's three multi-billion-dollar LNG projects designed to cash in on its North Field gas reserves -- the largest in the world.

It is a joint venture of the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation, which holds 65 percent and the U.S. Mobil Corporation and France's Total, which hold 10 percent each. Other partners are Mitsui Corp and Marubeni Corp, of Japan, which have 7.5 percent each.
